title: Mentoring the Junior Colleague Who Might Outpace Me
script: Hendra: [thoughtful] Nadia, can I say something that might sound strange coming from your supervisor? I think you're going to outgrow this role faster than either of us expected.
Nadia: That's not what I expected to hear in a mentoring session, honestly. Is that meant as a warning or a compliment?
Hendra: [carefully] Both, probably. It's flattering to mentor someone talented, and mildly unsettling to watch them approach the edge of what I can actually still teach them.
Nadia: I hadn't considered that mentoring someone might eventually become uncomfortable for the mentor, not just the mentee.
Hendra: [reflective] It rarely gets discussed, but there's a particular vanity in being needed, and a corresponding discomfort in becoming gradually less necessary.
Nadia: I don't think you're becoming less necessary. I still rely on your judgment for anything genuinely ambiguous.
Hendra: [honestly] Kind of you, though I suspect that reliance has an expiration date I should prepare for rather than resent when it arrives.
Nadia: What would preparing for it actually look like, in practical terms rather than abstract acceptance?
Hendra: [gently] Probably introducing you to people beyond this team, connections I've been quietly hoarding as though visibility were a finite resource I needed to ration.
Nadia: That would mean a great deal, though I want to be clear I'm not angling to replace you or rush past this role.
Hendra: [calmly] I know that. This isn't about insecurity regarding your intentions, it's about my own reluctance to relinquish being the most capable person in a given room.
Nadia: That's a strangely generous thing to admit to someone you're supposed to be advising, rather than confiding in.
Hendra: [encouraging] Good mentorship, I've come to think, requires admitting your own limitations openly enough that the mentee stops mistaking you for a ceiling.
Nadia: Then let's start there. Introduce me to whoever you've been protectively hoarding, and I'll try not to make you regret the generosity too quickly.
Hendra: [seriously] I'll hold you to that last part. Slowly, though. I'm allowed a transition period before you fully eclipse me.
